rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship's favourable sailing illustrates how people abuse relief after hardship, plotting against God's signs while unable to imagine punishment or understand its arrival.
rows.anchor: their ship of life is comfortably sailing in favourable winds. Hence, they are deeply engrossed in their pranks.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When seized, the deniers repent only during the trial; once rescued, they resume evil and arrogance, so warnings cannot benefit hearts covered in rust and such people face punishment.
rows.anchor: As soon as they are delivered from it, they will return to their evil ways: they will show the same arrogance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are told that rebellion's evil consequences fall on themselves; greater rebellion hastens God's conclusive communication of truth and brings punishment closer.
rows.anchor: None other but you will suffer the evil consequence of your rebelliousness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly-life parable continues the previous verse's description of brief worldly benefit: disbelievers are lured by it and imagine it secure and enduring.
rows.anchor: This is a parable of the life of this world referred to as “benefit from the life of this world for a few days”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtilāṭ means intermingling or intertwining and describes lush, dense vegetation produced when conducive rain falls.
rows.anchor: It signifies the lushness of vegetation and crops. This is because when conducive rain falls on them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayn means embellishment and beauty, came to denote varied vegetation, and the verbs izzayyana and tazayyana convey the same meaning.
rows.anchor: From here it came to be used for multifarious vegetation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr here means divine punishment.
rows.anchor: here refers to divine punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable warns people not to challenge God while intoxicated by comfort: crops and orchards can be ruined suddenly just when owners feel at their peak, as can the deniers.
rows.anchor: His order to punish them will be given right when they would think that they are in their prime.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observable signs of sudden ruin invite reflection; a sensible person learns from others' fate before helplessly experiencing punishment himself.
rows.anchor: Sensible is the person who learns from the fate of others not when he himself helplessly faces it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nations facing conclusive communication of truth are seized at their peak because faith and deeds matter more than material resources; resources hasten the fall of a morally bankrupt nation.
rows.anchor: the real importance before Him is that of faith and deeds and not of material resources.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abode of peace is Paradise, where there is neither regret about the past nor fear of the future; calling it peace contrasts with this world under God's constant grasp.
rows.anchor: that is the only place where a person will neither have any regret of the past nor fear of the future

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides those worthy of guidance according to His established practice, which is grounded in justice.
rows.anchor: God guides those who are worthy of it as per His established practice, which itself is based on justice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspecified additional reward is clarified by 6:160: one good deed brings tenfold reward.
rows.anchor: in verse 160 of S ūrah al-An‘ ām, it is explained that one good deed will entail ten times its reward.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahaqa means to overspread; qitr refers to the blackness of dust, here indicating the hopelessness that overtakes a person's face.
rows.anchor: Here concomitant indications show that this blackness is the one that overspreads a person’s face when he has totally lost hope.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating blackness and humiliation affirms their opposites: the believers' faces will be bright and fresh and they will receive honour.
rows.anchor: their faces will be shinning bright and fresh and at every step they will be treated with respect and honour.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evildoers' face-blackness is pictured as pieces of dark night because eternal helplessness produces hopelessness; the parenthetical warning means no one can rescue them from it.
rows.anchor: This shows blackness here refers to the blackness of hopelessness and because this blackness will be because of eternal helplessness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical warning also rules out help from the deities and intercessors the evildoers worshipped.
rows.anchor: All expectations of help and intercession from deities they had worshipped will be dashed to ground.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section IV follows the warning that none can save the deniers from God and explains their afterlife fate and how conjecture-based castles of desire collapse.
rows.anchor: In the coming verses, this fate they will encounter in the hereafter is described in detail.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's full knowledge of opponents' deeds reassures the Prophet and warns them; most reject truth, though some sensible people are mentioned in 10:42–43.
rows.anchor: The words “and God fully knows whatever they are doing” sound an assurance to the prophet and a warning to his opponents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After opponents demand a replacement or edited Qur'an, the discourse proves its divine origin from another angle, reassures the Prophet and companions, and substantiates Qur'anic claims.
rows.anchor: Now this same topic is taken up from another angle and it is proven that the Qur’ ān is the book of God

none: Qur'anic text and translation only; no separate author explanation.
Qur'anic text and translation only; no separate author explanation.
Qur'anic text and translation only; no separate author explanation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'wil means the manifestation of a report.
rows.anchor: means the manifestation of a news.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Book” means the Torah: its concise, vague prophecies required Qur'anic explanation, and the Qur'an completed and explained the religion entrusted to the final prophet.
rows.anchor: The prophecies of the Torah were in concise and vague form and needed explanation. The Qur’ān did this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic usage calls the Torah's scriptures the Book, includes the Gospel, uses plural books for parts and singular Book for the whole; before the Qur'an, the Torah held that status and other scriptures were its sections.
rows.anchor: All other scriptures had the status of being its chapters and sections.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers reject what their knowledge cannot yet grasp: the warned punishment has not appeared, and they demand a sample before accepting the Qur'an as divine.
rows.anchor: They wanted to see its sample before believing in it and accepting the Qur’ān as a divine book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's awareness of opponents assures the Prophet and warns them; the presence of believers shows sensible people remain, so they should be given time to believe and others lose their excuse before judgment.
rows.anchor: A requisite of this is that they be given time so that such people are given the opportunity to accept faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger's declaration of acquittal signals impending punishment: his presence protects his people, but after his departure that immunity ends and torment may come at any time.
rows.anchor: Once, he leaves them, they no longer have this immunity. The torment can now visit them anytime.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listening and looking passages reassure the Prophet that people of understanding remain, while those made deaf and blind by wrongdoing will not listen; God guides those who use innate faculties.
rows.anchor: He gives guidance to only those who use their innate faculties.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blindness passage repeats the same subject as the preceding passage about deaf listeners.
rows.anchor: mentions exactly the same topic as the one in the previous one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People make themselves deaf and blind by pursuing desires; God gave them the best abilities, and using them would reveal the prophetic call as the heart's own call.
rows.anchor: God has created human beings with the best of abilities. If they use them, they will feel that the call of the prophets

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection people will think their worldly stay brief and recognize one another as if constantly meeting; memories remain fresh, so treating worldly life as lengthy makes them heedless of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: Everything will be fresh in their minds as if it happened in not too distant a future.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When warned about the hereafter, the deniers paradoxically demand its arrival.
rows.anchor: Moreover, when he is warned of it, he starts demanding its arrival.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's established-practice discussion concerns a nation that collectively rejects its messenger and plans to kill him.
rows.anchor: if a messenger’s nation in its collective capacity decides to deny him and plans

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nation that collectively rejects and plots to kill its messenger is destroyed after the messenger and his nation are sifted apart; if many believe, decisive punishment is deferred to the hereafter.
rows.anchor: if there exist a substantial amount of believers in a nation, then instead of sending a decisive punishment to it, the punishment of the disbelievers among them is delayed to the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because many in Muhammad's nation believed, it escaped the decisive destruction suffered by ʿĀd and Thamūd; his enemies were killed in battles and will answer in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: it did not face a decisive punishment the way, the ‘ Ād, the Tham ūd etc faced.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation receives a messenger who delivers truth conclusively and establishes God's worldly court: believers triumph and persistent rejecters are routed; Quraysh faces this rule too.
rows.anchor: These messengers set up a court of justice in this world on behalf of God. Their fate is decided in this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger gives time to understand and reflect; those who persist in denial have their fate sealed under God's fully just decision.
rows.anchor: A messenger of God conclusively delivers the truth to his people and gives it the time needed to understand his message and reflect on it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This established punishment applies specifically to God's messengers, not prophets; it is not necessary for prophets to undergo it.
rows.anchor: this established practice only pertains to messengers of God and not to His prophets.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's first response to the mock demand makes clear that he has no control over when punishment arrives; the timing belongs to God.
rows.anchor: The first part of verse 49 is an answer to this demand from the tongue of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nation's deadline is measured by moral standards: God grants respite until rebellion reaches the point fixed for destruction, and only He knows the duration.
rows.anchor: when its rebelliousness reaches the stage that is fixed for its destruction, it is decimated by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the deniers wrongdoers underscores that criminals cannot reasonably demand punishment; believing only after it arrives is too late, and their own misdeeds make them unjust to themselves.
rows.anchor: those who are wrongdoers and who are going to be visited by this punishment in retribution of their crimes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth question parallels the earlier one in 10:48, but here rejection and mockery are overt; the blunt questioners receive an emphatic response suited to their temperament.
rows.anchor: The difference is that here the element of rejection and making fun that was downplayed there has become fully evident.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle rendered yes is a response particle used only before an oath; its emphatic answer asserts the Day of Judgement's certainty.
rows.anchor: is a particle of response and means g (yes) and only occurs before an oath.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The timing question posed through the Prophet is followed by a second question in verse 50.
rows.anchor: Their question about its time of arrival was given through the tongue of the prophet earlier. Now simultaneously another question is posed to them in verse 50.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claims that God gives life and death and that people return to Him substantiate the preceding argument through monotheism: God alone owns and rules the heavens and earth, so His promises will come true.
rows.anchor: This further substantiates through monotheism what is discussed earlier. No one has a share in the heavens and the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deities with no role in creation or death cannot rule the afterlife; the warning that most people do not know also conveys sorrow at their ignoring certain promises and warnings.
rows.anchor: How can those who have no share in creating and giving death become masters in the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse beginning at 10:37 refutes the claim that the Qur'an is fabricated, then addresses the doubts and confusions that prompted rejection.
rows.anchor: it began in verse 37 with the refutation of the disbelievers that this Book is a fabrication.
